key_insight: BEAKER introduces an expert-curated benchmark for evaluating AI models as the decision-making brains of self-driving chemical laboratories. It focuses on embodied laboratory capabilities rather than scientific knowledge alone.
problem_solved: Existing laboratory benchmarks emphasize safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving a gap in assessing how AI interprets laboratory scenes and supports experimental execution under real-world constraints.
method: Introduce an expert-curated benchmark aimed at embodied AI in self-driving chemical laboratories.
Frame evaluation around perceiving laboratory scenes, reasoning about experimental states, and acting within physical, procedural, and safety constraints.
Specific tasks, scoring methods, and evaluation results are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: BEAKER could help practitioners assess whether multimodal models are suitable for laboratory automation beyond answering scientific questions. The supplied excerpt does not establish model performance or demonstrated improvements.

paper_title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
